draft.title: Shares and dividends
card: Share
A share is one small part of the ownership of a company. People who own shares are called shareholders.
Dividend
A dividend is a share of a company's profit paid to shareholders. It is paid per share, so owning more shares means a bigger payment.
Dividend yield
Dividend yield = yearly dividend per share ÷ share price × 100%. It shows the yearly dividend as a percentage of the price.
Example: a share costs $40 and pays $1.80 in dividends over a year. Yield = 1.80 ÷ 40 × 100% = 4.5%.
draft.remember: Yield compares the yearly dividend with the share price, as a percentage.

a.q: A share costs $25 and pays a dividend of $1.50 over a year. What is the dividend yield?
a.why: Yield = 1.50 ÷ 25 × 100% = 6%. Dividing the price by the dividend gives 16.7%, which turns the fraction upside down.
a.clue: Divide the dividend by the share price.

b.q: Tariq owns 200 shares in a company. Each share costs $12 and the company pays $0.84 per share in a year. What is his total yearly dividend, and the yield?
b.why: Dividend = 200 × 0.84 = $168. Yield = 0.84 ÷ 12 × 100% = 7%. The yield uses the price and dividend of one share, so it does not depend on how many shares he owns, and $2400 is the cost of the shares.
b.clue: Yield uses one share, but the payment uses all 200.

problems.detail: The why says dividing the price by the dividend gives 16.7%. In fact 25 ÷ 1.50 = 16.7, which is 1667% once multiplied by 100%. The distractor works, but the explanation of where it comes from is loose.
